title: Money
purpose: Every site, worker, staff member, and partner is paid on the same accepted hours that the client pays for. There is a record behind every payment. Two names go on every large payment.
how: One number runs the whole chain. The client pays Vound for accepted hours. The client pays on net 30. That means the client pays 30 days after the invoice. Vound buys the data from KMSC. KMSC pays the sites, the workers, the staff, and the partners. Every step in the chain is paid on the same hours. These are the hours the client accepted after the month-end audit. Nobody in the chain is paid for an hour the client did not accept.

Accepted means kept. A reviewer watches every video before the client sees it. The verdict is keep, flag, or delete. Kept hours are paid. Flagged footage is deleted. It is never invoiced and never paid. The wearer log shows which person made each flagged video. The handbook sets the penalty. An operator pays 100 EGP for each fraudulent video. A Portfolio Manager pays 200 EGP. If the account is banned, or the fraud is systemic, an operator pays 250 EGP and a Portfolio Manager pays 500 EGP. A flag costs the site money. That is why it is better to catch a flag early.

Mano owns the money. Mano handles payroll, site and worker payments, partner payments, reimbursements, bonuses and referrals, and the daily and monthly numbers. All money questions go to Mano. Workers ask through their Portfolio Manager. Portfolio Managers and partners ask Mano directly. Every payment is prepared against a record. The record can be the wearer log, the QC verdicts, the site or partner agreement, or the offer letter. If there is no record, there is no payment.

Two names go on every large payment. If a payment is above the approval threshold, Adham signs second. Mano prepares the payment. Adham approves it. Both names are on the record before the money moves. Adham sets the threshold. The threshold is not written here. This rule protects Mano as much as it protects the money. Nobody can ask Mano to move a large sum alone. Nobody can blame Mano alone.

Month end always runs in the same order. In the last week of the month, Youssef Medhat runs the audit passes. Flagged footage is deleted. The invoice goes out on accepted hours only. Then Mano runs payroll, site payments, partner payments, and the referral and performance bonuses. Nothing is invoiced before the audit. Nobody is paid on a number the audit has not checked.

The month-end number is never a surprise. Every evening, the Portfolio Managers send their wrap reports. Mano puts them together into one number. The founders read that number at 8 PM. The daily number is the invoice growing day by day. The Sunday client update uses the same figure. Individual pay, targets, and bonus percentages are written in offer letters and nowhere else. The rules that apply to everyone are public.

procedures.name: Month-end close
procedures.owner: Mano, with Youssef Medhat and Adham
steps: In the last week of the month, Youssef Medhat runs the audit passes on every session. This happens before any hour is totaled.
Delete the flagged footage. Take those hours out first, per site and per account. Use the QC verdicts and the wearer log to find them.
Total the accepted hours. Mano gives that number to Adham. Adham sends the invoice on that number.
Run payroll, site payments, partner payments, and bonuses from the same number. Any payment above the threshold goes to Adham first.
Record the close: hours invoiced, hours paid, and flags deleted. Everyone works from one set of numbers.

procedures.name: Paying a site
procedures.owner: Mano, with the site's Portfolio Manager
steps: The payment terms are recorded with Mano when the deal closes, before launch day. Nobody changes the terms in the field.
At month end, take the site's accepted hours from the audit. The flagged hours are already taken out.
Prepare the payment against the site agreement. If the payment is above the threshold, Adham signs second.
Pay the site. Record the payment against the site. If the site owner has questions, they go to the Portfolio Manager first, then to Moharam, then to Adham.

procedures.name: Payroll
steps: Take each person's hours from the wearer log and the QC verdicts. Take out the flagged hours.
Apply the penalties from the handbook table. Each penalty must be tied to a session ID and a flag. Deductions for lost or damaged gear are applied only after Moharam reviews them.
Add the referral and performance bonuses the person earned this month.
Prepare the payroll run. Any payment above the threshold goes to Adham before it moves.
Pay at month end. Answer every pay question within 2 working days.

procedures.name: Paying a partner
steps: Count the partner's hours the same way we count our own hours. Use the QC verdicts and the wearer log. Take out the flagged footage first. Do this after the audit.
Check that nothing is holding the payment. A hold can be an open device count, a refused audit, or an exit where the phones are not back yet. The payment waits until the count matches.
Use the rate from the agreement and nothing else. If the payment is above the threshold, Adham signs second.
Pay after the invoice goes out. If a partner disputes the number, Moharam checks the facts and Adham handles the contract.

procedures.name: Second approval
steps: Prepare the payment with its record. The record says who is paid, what the payment is for, which hours or which agreement it is based on, and which month.
If the payment is above the threshold, send it to Adham before anything moves. Not after.
Adham approves the payment or asks questions. A spoken yes is not enough. The approval is kept with the payment record.
Never split a payment into smaller parts to stay under the threshold. Two payments to the same party in the same month count as one payment for this rule.

procedures.name: Reimbursements and referrals
steps: Reimbursements: send Mano the receipt, what you paid for, and which site it was for. Do this in the same week you paid.
Site referral: tell Mano the name of the business, the location, and your contact person before the first meeting. The reward is 10% when the contract closes.
Hire referral: give Mano the person's name, phone number, and role before the person is hired. The reward is 2,000 EGP once the person is onboarded and working.
Mano answers every request within 2 working days. Rewards are paid with the month's payroll.

procedures.name: Final pay on leaving
steps: Every phone, mount, cap, and charger goes back to the Portfolio Manager or to Mano within 24 hours of the person leaving.
The Portfolio Manager inspects each item and ticks its condition: screen, port, mount, battery. The registry is updated the same day.
Any deduction follows the handbook. It is applied only after Moharam reviews it.
Mano releases the final pay after the inspection. Never before.

breaks.what: The client rejects hours we invoiced
breaks.do: Adham handles the conversation with the client. Nobody else talks to the client. Youssef Medhat matches the rejected sessions against our verdicts the same day. Any hours the client does not accept are also taken out of what we pay the sites, workers, staff, and partners. That is what it means to be paid net of fraud flags.

breaks.what: A worker says their pay is wrong
breaks.do: This goes to Mano. Mano answers within 2 working days. Bring the worker's name and role, the month, the amount they expected, and the amount they received. Mano checks the wearer log and the verdicts. If the worker disputes a flag, the flag goes to Youssef Medhat. If he reverses the flag, the pay is corrected.

breaks.what: A large payment is ready and Adham has not signed
breaks.do: The payment waits. Adham reads the number every evening, Egypt time, and the sync happens every day. So the wait is hours, not weeks. A late payment can be explained. A wrong payment cannot be taken back.

breaks.what: Someone asks Mano to move money without a record
breaks.do: The answer is no. Every payment has a record: who is paid, what the payment is for, and which hours or which agreement it is based on. Mano says no once and tells Adham the same day. If someone puts pressure on the person who holds the money, that is a problem for the founders to handle, not for Mano.

Moharam checks the facts. Mano handles the money. Adham handles the contract. All of this happens the same day. The record is the QC verdicts and the wearer log. The payment waits while any device count is open.

breaks.what: A site owner wants to be paid for rejected hours
breaks.do: The agreement says the site is paid for accepted hours. The site owner signed it before launch day. The Portfolio Manager shows the site owner which sessions were flagged and why. Then the site can help catch the problem next month. If the site owner keeps pushing, Moharam handles it the same day. If it becomes a contract question, Adham handles it.

breaks.what: Someone leaves and the gear is not back
breaks.do: The final pay waits. The Portfolio Manager chases the gear within 24 hours. After 24 hours, the phone goes into MDM lost mode, following the asset control rules, and Moharam gets a report. Deductions follow the handbook, after Moharam reviews them.
Adham chases the client. Nobody else contacts the client. Mano raises it at the executive sync on the day the net 30 deadline passes. Mano brings the invoice number and the amount.

training: Mano learns the chain, the month-end order, and the threshold rule. Mano has one session with Adham before the first close that Mano runs alone.

Portfolio Managers, in their first week, learn three things. How a flag becomes a deduction. What the wearer log does to pay. And the answer to every pay question a worker asks at the site: go to Mano, and Mano answers within 2 working days.
Operators, on day one, learn three things. They are paid on accepted hours. A flag costs the site money. And the rule 'before you take the hat off, tap stop' is a pay rule too.
Youssef Medhat and the reviewers learn that a verdict is a payment decision. The audit passes run in the last week of the month. The invoice waits for them.

questions.a: At month end, through Mano. You are paid on your accepted hours, with the flagged hours taken out. You are not paid before the audit.

questions.q: Why is my pay less than my hours?
questions.a: Because of flags, or because of a penalty from the handbook table. Ask Mano. Tell Mano the month, the amount you expected, and the amount you received. If you disagree with a flag, Youssef Medhat decides on it.

questions.q: Can I know what someone else is paid?
questions.a: No. Individual pay is written in offer letters. The rules that apply to everyone are on this page.

questions.q: Who sets the threshold, and what is it?
questions.a: Adham sets it. It is not published. If Mano says a payment needs a second signature, the rule is working. It is not a delay.

questions.q: I referred a site. When do I get the 10%?
questions.a: When the contract closes. Mano pays it. Tell Mano before the first meeting, so the referral is on record.

principle: Every site, worker, staff member, and partner is paid on accepted hours, with the fraud flags taken out. The company is paid the same way.

approval.rule: Any payment above the approval threshold needs a second signature from Adham before the money moves.
approval.note: Two names go on every large payment. Nobody can ask Mano to move a large sum alone. Nobody can blame Mano alone.

monthEnd.text: In the last week of the month. Every audit pass is finished before any hour is totaled.
Flagged footage is deleted. It is never sent, never invoiced, and never paid.
The invoice counts accepted hours only. It does not go out before the audit is done.
Payroll, site payments, partner payments, and referral and performance bonuses. If a payment is above the threshold, Adham signs second.
